title: Copilot Studio: labelled and encrypted file uploads for agents on the Microsoft 365 channel
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the planned labelled-upload support from today's documented encrypted-file restriction, and its licensing and commands are supported. Two control paths reach the right page but should explain the remaining steps to configure label blocking and encryption permissions.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Scope: Existing file-input setting; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how planned labelled-file support interacts with the existing File uploads setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio labelled encrypted upload enable default prerequisites MPIP Microsoft 365 channel 571305. Read image-input-analysis: existing File uploads is documented, but encrypted files remain unsupported and the planned setting interaction is not described.

claims.claim: Today's file-input documentation says encrypted files, including sensitivity-label encryption and password protection, are unsupported.
claims.quote: Files with encryption, such as sensitivity labels or password protection, aren't supported.

claims.claim: For encrypted or password-protected Office uploads, the agent tells the user the file cannot be read.
claims.quote: When a user uploads a password-protected or encrypted Office file, the agent tells the user that the file is encrypted or password-protected and can't be read.

claims.claim: Some rights-managed or label-encrypted uploads instead produce a generic error.
claims.quote: For some rights-managed or label-encrypted files, the agent returns a generic error instead.

claims.claim: The file-input article describes agents powered by the standard harness.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: The file-input page points users to Microsoft Copilot Chat, which supports sensitivity-labelled files.
claims.quote: use a Microsoft 365 experience such as Microsoft Copilot Chat, which supports sensitivity-labeled files.

claims.claim: Connecting the Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels makes an agent available in Teams and Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: After you publish your agent at least once, you can connect it to the Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels so users can chat with it in both Teams and Microsoft Copilot.

claims.claim: For sensitivity-label encryption in the documented AI scenarios, users need EXTRACT as well as VIEW for data to be returned.
claims.quote: When the sensitivity label applies encryption, users must have the EXTRACT usage right, as well as VIEW, for the AI apps to return the data.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: EXTRACT determines whether Copilot or agents can display text from encrypted content in the documented general scenarios.
claims.quote: The usage right that grants permission to copy text is EXTRACT, with the more user-friendly, common name of Copy. It's this usage right that determines whether Copilot or agents can display text to the user from encrypted content.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[3].note
claims.claim: The person applying encryption always has EXTRACT as Rights Management owner.
claims.quote: The person applying the encryption always has the EXTRACT usage right, because they are the Rights Management owner.

claims.claim: Full control (OWNER) includes EXTRACT.
claims.quote: Because the Full control (OWNER) usage right includes all the usage rights, EXTRACT is automatically included with Full control.

claims.claim: A user's effective usage rights can differ from the applied label's configured permissions.
claims.quote: Most times, when the content is labeled, the usage rights granted to the user match those from the sensitivity label configuration. However, there are some situations that can result in the content's usage rights being different from the applied label configuration

claims.claim: The Purview Copilot Studio page says encryption is supported only with sensitivity labels and only for SharePoint knowledge sources.
claims.quote: Encryption is supported only with sensitivity labels, and only for the SharePoint knowledge source.

claims.claim: The SharePoint troubleshooting page instead says agents cannot extract or ground on encrypted content.
claims.quote: However, the agent can't extract or ground on content whose protection encrypts the file. This limitation includes sensitivity labels that apply encryption, Double Key Encryption (DKE), and password-protected files.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Flows, connectors and tools can pass an uploaded file to downstream systems such as SharePoint and ServiceNow.
claims.quote: Optionally, you can add logic in your flow to send this file to SharePoint, ServiceNow, Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and similar services.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a sensitivity-label check at the uploaded-file hand-off to downstream tools.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio uploaded file sensitivity label check downstream flow connector protection. Opened guidance/pass-files-to-connectors and image-input-analysis; read purview/ai-copilot-studio. No label check at that hand-off is described.

claims.claim: The upload-specific identity model has not been documented beyond the roadmap's user/agent permissions wording.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio MPIP sensitivity labelled encrypted file uploads Microsoft 365 channel default licensing switch EXTRACT. Read roadmap, image-input-analysis, publication-add-bot-to-microsoft-teams and purview/ai-copilot-studio; no planned upload-specific identity model.

claims.claim: Copilot and agents generally cannot access unopened SharePoint and OneDrive documents encrypted with user-defined permissions, subject to two stated exceptions.
claims.quote: Copilot and agents can't access unopened documents in SharePoint and OneDrive when they're labeled and encrypted with user-defined permissions

claims.claim: One exception is a default sensitivity label extending SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents, with EXTRACT required.
claims.quote: unless the label is used as a default sensitivity label that extends SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents or they're directly referenced by typing "/" (and in both cases, the user has EXTRACT permissions).

claims.claim: The other exception is directly referencing the document by typing '/', again requiring EXTRACT.
claims.quote: or they're directly referenced by typing "/" (and in both cases, the user has EXTRACT permissions).

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Purview documents label-based Copilot DLP restrictions for Copilot Studio agents when their knowledge source is SharePoint.
claims.quote: When the knowledge source is SharePoint, a DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can restrict agents built in Copilot Studio for Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 Copilot from processing sensitive content based on a specified sensitivity label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: DLP does not scan the contents of files uploaded directly into Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts.
claims.quote: DLP can't scan the contents of files that you upload directly into prompts, so evaluation of the uploaded file for sensitive data doesn't occur. DLP only checks the text you type into the prompt itself.

claims.claim: Coverage of planned labelled-file uploads to agents by label-based Copilot DLP has not been documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio uploaded file sensitivity label check downstream flow connector protection; Copilot Studio MPIP sensitivity labelled encrypted file uploads Microsoft 365 channel default licensing switch EXTRACT. Read ai-copilot-studio and dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-learn-about.

claims.claim: The Purview DLP path reaches the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location in the custom policy wizard.
claims.quote: Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy. 3. Select the Custom template, then Custom policy. 4. On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
claims.fix: Keep the existing path and add to controls[2].note: 'Add a rule with Content contains > Sensitivity labels and the Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content action.' The cited page's Supported conditions and actions table documents the remaining label-blocking control.

claims.claim: The printed New-DLPCompliancePolicy and New-DLPComplianceRule calls create the documented Copilot label-processing restriction with $loc and $advrule defined first.
claims.quote:
New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name "Copilot Policy" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences")
New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The label-based DLP rule uses Content contains > Sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: create DLP policies that use the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy location with the Content contains > Sensitivity labels condition to exclude items from being processed.

claims.claim: The Purview Data Security AI Admin role can create or edit Copilot-location DLP policies.
claims.quote: Accounts with one of the following roles or role groups can create or edit a DLP policy for the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location: ... Purview Data Security AI Admin

claims.claim: The label-encryption path starts at the Purview portal and reaches Access control through the label scope and Control access option.
claims.quote: make sure the Files & other data assets option is selected for the label's scope ... on the Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected page, make sure you select Control access. ... On the Access control page
claims.fix: The already-cited create-sensitivity-labels page supplies Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > label > Edit label > Define the scope for this label. Append ' > Configure access control settings > Assign permissions now' to the current path. Add to controls[3].note: 'To set individual rights, assign the intended users or groups and select Choose permissions.' These remaining steps are on https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels.

claims.claim: On Access control, Configure access control settings exposes the Assign permissions now choice.
claims.quote: When you select Configure access control settings on the Access control page to create or edit a sensitivity label, choose one of the following options: - Assign permissions now

claims.claim: EXTRACT is displayed in the Purview portal as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, the EXTRACT usage right is displayed as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label> -EncryptionEnabled $true -EncryptionProtectionType Template -EncryptionRightsDefinitions <rights> configures template-based label encryption and rights.
claims.quote: The EncryptionRightsDefinitions parameter specifies the rights users have when accessing protected. ... This parameter is meaningful only when the EncryptionEnabled parameter value is either $true or $false and the EncryptionProtectionType parameter value is Template.

claims.claim: The Purview portal route to enable sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive is Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Turn on now.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels. 2. If you see a message to turn on the ability to process content in Office online files, select Turn on now

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true enables sensitivity-label support in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: To enable the new capabilities, use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the EnableAIPIntegration parameter: ... Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true

claims.claim: Enabling SharePoint and OneDrive sensitivity-label support through the portal requires a global administrator.
claims.quote: You must sign in as a global administrator for your tenant.

claims.claim: Multi-Geo tenants must use PowerShell to enable sensitivity-label support across all geo-locations.
claims.quote: If you have Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo, you must use PowerShell to enable these capabilities for all your geo-locations.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive sensitivity-label enablement is documented for files stored in those services, not for planned agent uploads.
claims.quote: Enable built-in labeling for supported Office files and PDF files in SharePoint and OneDrive

claims.claim: The Copilot experiences & agents summary report is at Purview portal > Solutions > DSPM for AI (classic) > Reports > Copilot experiences & agents.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > DSPM for AI (classic) ... navigate to the Reports page to view the results of your policy. Select Copilot experiences & agents

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation for the DSPM for AI Copilot experiences & agents summary report is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: DSPM for AI Copilot experiences agents summary report API export PowerShell. Opened ai-copilot-studio and Export-ActivityExplorerData; results document portal summary and activity exports, not automation of that summary report.

claims.claim: Underlying Activity Explorer activities can be exported with Export-ActivityExplorerData.
claims.quote: Use the Export-ActivityExplorerData cmdlet to export activities from Data classification > Activity Explorer in the Microsoft 365 Purview compliance portal.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends waiting at least a day for policy data before reviewing the report.
claims.quote: Wait at least a day for data, and then navigate to the Reports page to view the results of your policy.

claims.claim: The published generative-answer feature rate is 2 Copilot Credits, subject to the stated licensed-usage inclusion.
claims.quote: | Generative answer^2^ | 2 Copilot Credits | No charge |

claims.claim: Classic answers, generative answers and Microsoft Graph tenant grounding in Copilot Chat, Teams or SharePoint are not charged when the agent uses the authenticated identity of a Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed user.
claims.quote: If you have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, using agents in Copilot Chat, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint for classic answers, generative answers, or Microsoft Graph tenant grounding isn't charged when the agent runs with your authenticated identity.
